correctness.rationale: A generic section crosses between 3 and 5 of the nine edges. Direct integration of the intersection of the two triangular-facet and three lateral-face offset constraints gives the pentagon measure; equilateral dihedral azimuth symmetry reduces it to a 1D elementary primitive Psi(x), yielding p5=12Psi/[pi(3+2x)]. Expected number of crossed edges determines p3, p4. The derivative Psi'(x)=pi/6-xB(x)/sqrt(1+x^2) and Psi''(x)=[T(x)-B(x)]/(1+x^2)^(3/2) with increasing T and decreasing B imply exactly one sign transition of D(x)=(3+2x)Psi'-2Psi, hence unique pentagon maximum. Analytically bracketed optimizer near .47287604788115; independently integrated the arbitrary-prism angle-gap representation at six heights including small and large values and compared the elementary closed formula to <4e-10, not an all-heights numerical proof.
